hello.note: Said with palms pressed together. More formal: नमस्कार (namaskaar).

goodbye.note: नमस्ते (namaste) also works when leaving. अलविदा (alvida) is only for final, dramatic farewells.

please.note: Formal. In speech, politeness usually comes from the -iye verb ending (बैठिए, baithiye) or English 'please'.

youre_welcome.note: Hindi has no set reply to thanks; this ('it's nothing') is the natural one.

yes.note: Politer: जी हाँ (ji haan) or just जी (ji).

no.note: Politer: जी नहीं (ji nahin). Casual: ना (na).

sorry.note: English 'sorry' (सॉरी) is also very common in everyday speech.

excuse_me.note: Literally 'please listen' — the usual way to call a stranger or a waiter.

good_morning.note: Formal. Day to day, people say नमस्ते (namaste) or गुड मॉर्निंग (good morning).

how_are_you.note: To a woman: आप कैसी हैं? (aap kaisi hain?)

im_fine.note: To ask back: और आप? (aur aap?)

whats_your_name.note: Extra respectful, e.g. to an elder: आपका शुभ नाम? (aapka shubh naam?)

my_name_is.note: The verb है (hai, 'is') comes at the end, after the name.

nice_to_meet_you.note: Also common: आपसे मिलकर अच्छा लगा (aapse milkar achchha laga).

im_from.note: से (se, 'from') comes after the place: मैं भारत से हूँ (main Bhaarat se hoon).

speak_english.note: Literally 'does English come to you?' Many people say इंग्लिश (english) instead of अंग्रेज़ी.

dont_understand.note: To ask for a repeat: फिर से बोलिए (phir se boliye).

speak_slowly.note: In speech often without कृपया — the -iye ending is already polite.

where.note: ँ (chandrabindu) nasalises the vowel: the n in kahan is not fully pronounced.

what.note: On its own it can sound blunt; to ask someone to repeat, say जी? (ji?).

how_much.note: Also: इसका दाम क्या है? (iska daam kya hai?)

where_bathroom.note: Also common: बाथरूम (bathroom), वॉशरूम (washroom). Signs say शौचालय (shauchaalay).

can_you_help.text: क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकते हैं?
can_you_help.roman: kya aap meri madad kar sakte hain?
can_you_help.note: To a woman: क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकती हैं? (kya aap meri madad kar sakti hain?)

what_time.note: Very common too: टाइम क्या हुआ है? (time kya hua hai?)

six.note: Devanagari digit: ६. Usually pronounced 'chhe'; also spelled छः.

eight.note: Devanagari digit: ८. ठ is a tongue-curled t with a puff of air, not English 'th'.

tea.note: Order it as एक चाय (ek chai); it comes with milk and sugar unless you ask otherwise.

bread.note: रोटी is Indian flatbread. Sliced loaf bread is ब्रेड (bread) or डबल रोटी (double roti).

menu_please.note: Literally 'please show the menu'. Many say मेन्यू कार्ड (menu card).

delicious.note: Very common in speech: बहुत टेस्टी है! (bahut tasty hai!)

no_meat.note: A woman says: मैं मांस नहीं खाती (main maans nahin khaati). Also: मैं शाकाहारी हूँ (main shaakaahaari hoon).

enjoy_meal.note: Hindi has no fixed 'bon appétit'; hosts say this. Formal: भोजन का आनंद लीजिए (bhojan ka aanand lijiye).

left.note: Turn left: बाएँ मुड़िए (baayen mudiye). Drivers also say लेफ़्ट (left).

right.note: Turn right: दाएँ मुड़िए (daayen mudiye). Drivers also say राइट (right).

stop_here.note: Drivers are often called भैया (bhaiya, 'brother'): भैया, यहीं रोक दीजिए.

airport.note: In everyday speech most people say एयरपोर्ट (airport).

hotel.note: In many places होटल can also mean a simple restaurant.

want_to_go.note: No word for 'to' is needed: मुझे दिल्ली जाना है (mujhe Dilli jaana hai).

is_it_far.note: How far is it? कितनी दूर है? (kitni door hai?)

one_ticket.note: Return ticket: आने-जाने का टिकट (aane-jaane ka ticket).

too_expensive.note: When bargaining, add: थोड़ा कम कीजिए (thoda kam kijiye), 'bring it down a bit'.

cheaper.note: Also: कुछ सस्ता दिखाइए (kuchh sasta dikhaaiye), 'show me something cheaper'.

id_like_this.note: When buying, also: यह दे दीजिए (yeh de dijiye).

just_looking.note: A woman says: मैं बस देख रही हूँ (main bas dekh rahi hoon).

pay_card.text: क्या कार्ड से पेमेंट हो सकता है?
pay_card.roman: kya card se payment ho sakta hai?
pay_card.note: Casual and very common: कार्ड चलेगा? (card chalega?)

cash.note: In speech, कैश (cash) is just as common.

open.note: Many shop signs in India simply say OPEN in English.

big.note: बड़ी (badi) with feminine nouns. ड़ is a quick flap of the tongue, between d and r.

tomorrow.note: Same word as 'yesterday'; the verb tense decides: कल मिलेंगे (kal milenge) = see you tomorrow.

yesterday.note: Same word as 'tomorrow'; the verb tense decides: कल बारिश हुई (kal baarish hui) = it rained yesterday.

now.note: अभी is 'right now'; अब (ab) is 'now' as in 'from now on'.

good_evening.note: Formal (TV, speeches). In daily life people just say नमस्ते (namaste) in the evening too.

good_night.note: In everyday speech: गुड नाइट (good night).

see_you_later.note: Also: फिर मिलते हैं (phir milte hain).

call_police.note: Polite form: पुलिस को बुलाइए (police ko bulaaiye). Emergency number in India: 112.

need_doctor.note: Also: डॉक्टर को बुलाइए (doctor ko bulaaiye), 'please call a doctor'.

im_lost.note: A woman says: मैं रास्ता भटक गई हूँ (main raasta bhatak gayi hoon).

pharmacy.note: Signs usually say केमिस्ट (chemist) or मेडिकल स्टोर (medical store).

lost_phone.note: If it was stolen: मेरा फ़ोन चोरी हो गया है (mera phone chori ho gaya hai).

be_careful.note: Also: संभलकर! (sambhalkar!). Warning signs say सावधान (saavdhaan).

no_problem.note: Also very common: कोई बात नहीं (koi baat nahin).

dont_know.note: Shorter and casual: पता नहीं (pata nahin).

i_like_it.note: Also: मुझे अच्छा लगा (mujhe achchha laga), 'I liked it'.

im_tired.note: A woman says: मैं थक गई हूँ (main thak gayi hoon).

welcome.note: Warm and very common at the door: आइए, आइए! (aaiye, aaiye!)

my_family.note: Casual: मेरे घरवाले (mere gharvaale), 'my folks at home'.

mother.note: The n only nasalises the vowel. Many say मम्मी (mummy); respectful: माताजी (maataji).

brother.note: Older brother: भैया (bhaiya). भाई is also a friendly way to address any man.

sister.note: Older sister: दीदी (didi), also a polite way to address a young woman.

child.note: Son: बेटा (beta), daughter: बेटी (beti). Plural: बच्चे (bachche).

friend.note: Same word for a woman. Between women, a female friend is also सहेली (saheli).

this_is_my_friend.note: A female friend: यह मेरी दोस्त है (yeh meri dost hai).

are_you_married.text: क्या आपकी शादी हो गई है?
are_you_married.roman: kya aapki shaadi ho gayi hai?
are_you_married.note: Also: क्या आप शादीशुदा हैं? (kya aap shaadishuda hain?)

monday.note: On Monday: सोमवार को (somvaar ko). Every day name ends in -वार (vaar), 'day'.

thursday.note: Also: बृहस्पतिवार (brihaspativaar) and, in the north-west, वीरवार (veervaar).

friday.note: Also heard, especially among Muslims: जुम्मा (jumma).

sunday.note: Also very common: इतवार (itvaar), and English संडे (sunday).

weekend.note: Formal Hindi: सप्ताहांत (saptaahaant), rarely heard in speech.

what_day.note: For the date: आज कौन सी तारीख है? (aaj kaun si taareekh hai?)

eleven.note: Devanagari digits: ११. Hindi numbers 11–99 are irregular, so each one is learned on its own.

hundred.note: Devanagari digits: १००. Also said एक सौ (ek sau).

thousand.note: Devanagari digits: १०००. Also एक हज़ार (ek hazaar). 1,00,000 is एक लाख (ek laakh).

how_old.note: Also: आप कितने साल के हैं? (aap kitne saal ke hain?); to a woman, की (ki) replaces के (ke).

years_old.note: A woman says: मैं … साल की हूँ (main … saal ki hoon).

red.note: Never changes its ending, whatever the noun.

white.note: Like लाल (laal), it never changes its ending.

what_colour.note: For a feminine noun: यह किस रंग की है? (yeh kis rang ki hai?)

this_one.note: For a feminine item: यह वाली (yeh vaali).

that_one.note: For a feminine item: वह वाली (voh vaali). वह is often spelled वो (vo), as it is said.

another_one.note: Short and common: एक और (ek aur).

its_hot.note: Without बहुत (bahut, 'very'): गर्मी है. Hot food or water is गरम (garam).

its_cold.note: Without बहुत (bahut, 'very'): ठंड है. Cold food or water is ठंडा (thanda).

its_sunny.note: Literally 'the sunshine has come out'. Harsh sun: तेज़ धूप है (tez dhoop hai).

its_windy.note: Also: आज बहुत हवा है (aaj bahut hava hai).

beautiful_day.note: A warmer word for pleasant weather: सुहाना (suhaana), as in मौसम सुहाना है (mausam suhaana hai).

summer.note: Also means 'heat'. In summer: गर्मियों में (garmiyon mein).

winter.note: Also means 'cold', even a head cold. In winter: सर्दियों में (sardiyon mein).

have_reservation.note: Literally 'there's a booking in my name'. रिज़र्वेशन (reservation) is mostly used for trains.

room.note: Hotels also say रूम (room). Any rooms free? कमरा मिलेगा? (kamra milega?)

check_out_time.note: Also: चेक-आउट का टाइम क्या है? (check-out ka time kya hai?)

map.note: On phones people say मैप (map): मैप पर दिखाइए (map par dikhaaiye), 'show me on the map'.

bus.note: Bus station: बस अड्डा (bus adda). Same spelling as बस (bas), 'enough, just'.

next_train.note: Railway staff and older people often call a train गाड़ी (gaadi).

is_this_seat_free.note: Also: यहाँ कोई बैठा है? (yahan koi baitha hai?), 'is anyone sitting here?'

what_do_you_do.note: To a woman: आप क्या करती हैं? (aap kya karti hain?)

i_work_in.note: A woman says: मैं … में काम करती हूँ (main … mein kaam karti hoon).

im_student.note: A woman says: मैं छात्रा हूँ (main chhaatra hoon). Very common: मैं स्टूडेंट हूँ (main student hoon).

office.note: In everyday speech ऑफ़िस (office) is just as common.

meeting.note: Formal Hindi: बैठक (baithak). I'm in a meeting: मैं मीटिंग में हूँ (main meeting mein hoon).

im_busy.note: In casual speech: मैं बिज़ी हूँ (main busy hoon).

day_off.note: Also a holiday or leave. To take a day off: छुट्टी लेना (chhutti lena).

colleague.note: Same word for a woman. In speech, कलीग (colleague) is common.

lets_start.note: Casual: चलो, शुरू करें (chalo, shuru karen).

good_job.note: To a child or junior: शाबाश! (shaabaash!)

table_for_two.text: दो लोगों के लिए एक टेबल चाहिए
table_for_two.roman: do logon ke liye ek table chaahiye
table_for_two.note: Politer as a question: दो लोगों के लिए टेबल मिलेगी? (do logon ke liye table milegi?)

what_recommend.note: Also: यहाँ की स्पेशल डिश क्या है? (yahan ki special dish kya hai?)

not_spicy.note: Or: मिर्च कम डालिए (mirch kam daaliye), 'go easy on the chilli'.

vegetarian_food.note: Menus and signs say वेज (veg) and नॉन-वेज (non-veg); a green dot marks veg food.

no_sugar.note: Ordering tea: बिना चीनी की चाय (bina cheeni ki chai). Many also say शुगर (sugar).

im_full.note: To a host who keeps serving: बस, बस! (bas, bas!)

takeaway.note: Also very common: पार्सल कर दीजिए (parcel kar dijiye).

it_was_delicious.note: Warm and very common: मज़ा आ गया! (maza aa gaya!)

keep_change.note: Small change is छुट्टे (chhutte): छुट्टे हैं? (chhutte hain?), 'do you have change?'

head.note: Short i as in 'sit', with a tapped r; not like English 'sir'.

stomach.note: Stomach ache: पेट में दर्द (pet mein dard).

head_hurts.note: Also very common: सिर दर्द हो रहा है (sir dard ho raha hai).

medicine.note: Also दवा (dava). A tablet is गोली (goli).

call_ambulance.note: Polite form: एम्बुलेंस बुलाइए (ambulance bulaaiye). In India dial 108 or 112.

dentist.note: In cities also डेंटिस्ट (dentist). Toothache: दाँत में दर्द (daant mein dard).

need_rest.note: Also: मुझे आराम की ज़रूरत है (mujhe aaraam ki zaroorat hai).

feel_better.note: Also: अब मैं पहले से ठीक हूँ (ab main pehle se theek hoon).

get_well.note: To a friend: जल्दी ठीक हो जाओ! (jaldi theek ho jaao!)

lets_meet.note: To fix a time: कब मिलें? (kab milen?), 'when shall we meet?'

are_you_free.note: Also: क्या कल आपके पास समय है? (kya kal aapke paas samay hai?)

call_me.note: Also common: मुझे कॉल कीजिए (mujhe call kijiye).

your_number.note: Often: अपना नंबर दीजिए (apna number dijiye), 'give me your number'.

have_nice_day.note: Formal: आपका दिन शुभ हो! (aapka din shubh ho!)

good_luck.note: Before an exam or interview people usually say ऑल द बेस्ट! (all the best!)

happy_birthday.note: Also: जन्मदिन की शुभकामनाएँ! (janamdin ki shubhkaamnaayen!). The song is sung in English.

miss_you.note: Literally 'your memory comes to me'. To an elder: आपकी (aapki) instead of तुम्हारी.
